<description>
Before taking a peer's next message, `ProcessMessages` calls `ProcessOrphanTx` to reconsider that peer's orphan transactions. `ProcessOrphanTx` takes `cs_main` first, even when the peer has no orphan work, which is the usual case. As a result, the message handler takes `cs_main` for every peer on every pass, even when the peer sent nothing or only messages that never need it, such as `ping`.

This PR checks for orphan work under `m_tx_download_mutex` first and returns without taking `cs_main` when there is none. When there is orphan work, the existing path runs unchanged.

Part of the cs_main contention reduction effort that leads to #36244. This PR is independent of the others in that effort, so it can be reviewed and merged on its own.

#### Motivation

In #36244, a worker thread holds `cs_main` while it validates blocks, and the message handler should not wait for validation just to learn that a peer has no orphan work.

Even without #36244, this PR removes a `cs_main` acquisition from every `ProcessMessages` call for a peer without orphan work. The message handler makes that call for each peer on every pass of its loop, at least every 100 ms, whether or not the peer sent anything. So the handler contends less with validation, RPC and wallet threads. Each pass still takes `cs_main` in `SendMessages`.

#### Measurement

A `ping` is handled while another thread holds `cs_main` for 50 ms. Release builds of master `66776840be` and this PR, run alternately; median over 21 pings, median of 3 runs:

| | master | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `ProcessMessages` time, no contention | 0.005 ms | 0.005 ms |
| `ProcessMessages` time while another thread holds `cs_main` | 50.1 ms | 0.02 ms |

This measures the message step only: the `pong` is queued without waiting. On master, the same handler pass then calls `SendMessages`, which still takes `cs_main`, so a busy `cs_main` still delays the pass for other peers. The end-to-end gain comes with #36244, whose `SendMessages` does not wait either.

#### Cost

A peer that does have orphan work pays one extra `m_tx_download_mutex` lock and lookup per message.

#### Testing

`process_messages_without_orphan_work` checks that `ProcessMessages` completes for a peer with no orphan work while another thread holds `cs_main`. It fails without this change.
</description>
